Per-head formulas, pruned — ParT’s selection kept

ParT_full · JetClass · ParT’s class attention written per head. A head applies one rule to every jet: a score for each particle → attention weights by softmax (with the class token’s own share) → a sum over the particles of a formula of each particle’s physics (16 value neurons). ParT’s fixed arithmetic after the heads turns the 256 head outputs into the class scores.

same class as ParT (test)93.30%accuracy0.8435ParT 0.8603AUC0.9847ParT 0.9877
Kept of ParT: Both class blocks’ attention weights (which particles each head looks at, per jet) are ParT’s, computed from its particle blocks.
Kept in every model: ParT’s fixed arithmetic after the heads — out-projection, per-head scale, LayerNorms, the 128→512→128 MLP with residuals in both class blocks, the final LayerNorm and the last layer. Not fitted, no physics content: a smooth map from the 256 head outputs to the 10 class scores.
Formulas: Every head’s value — what it sums over the particles it attends to — is a formula of each particle’s own physics. Pruned: each head keeps only the inputs it needs (17–29 of 38), re-tuned.

Notation

jet, particlesa jet has n particles i = 1…n (up to 128); x_i = the per-particle inputs of particle i (defined in the table at the bottom).
class tokenParT’s learned 128-number vector c that “reads” the jet. In class block 1 it is a constant (the same for every jet); class block 2 reads with the output of block 1.
class blocks b, heads hParT ends with 2 class-attention blocks (b = 1, 2), each with 8 heads (h = 1…8): 16 heads in total.
score s_bhihow strongly head h of block b looks at particle i: s_bhi = q_bh · k_bhi / 4, with q_bh = W_q,bh · c (the query of the class token) and k_bhi = W_k,bh · LN(e_i) (the key of particle i; e_i its embedding after ParT’s 8 particle blocks, LN a LayerNorm). The class token has its own score s_bh0 = q_bh · k_bh0.
attention weight α_bhiα_bhi = exp(s_bhi) / Σ_{j=0…n} exp(s_bhj), i = 0 (the class token itself) … n: a softmax over [class token, particles] of this jet; the n + 1 weights of a head sum to 1. Per jet and per head.
terms t(x)for every input x_f: x_f itself and max(0, x_f − θ_f,k) at 5 thresholds θ_f,1…5 (the 15–85 % quantiles of x_f over particles): 6 terms per input.
value neuron o_bh,mm = 1…16: o_bh,m = Σ_{i=1…n} α_bhi · f_bh,m(x_i) + c_bh,m · α_bh0 + b_bh,m, with f_bh,m(x) = Σ_terms w · t(x): a sum over the particles, weighted by the head’s attention, of a formula of each particle’s inputs; plus the class token’s share α_bh0 times a constant.
ParT_downstreamthe 16 × 16 = 256 head outputs o go through ParT’s own fixed operations: out-projection, per-head scale, LayerNorm, residual and a 128→512→128 MLP in each class block, the final LayerNorm and the last layer → 10 class scores. Not fitted.

What the output is composed of

for every jet:
    X[i, :]          = the per-particle inputs of particle i (definitions at the bottom of the page)
    for each class block b (1, 2) and head h (1..8):
        alpha[b, h, :]  = ParT's attention weights over [class token, particles]            # kept from ParT
        o[b, h, :]      = sum_i alpha[b, h, i] * f_bh(X[i, :]) + alpha_cls * c_bh + bias_bh   # 16 value neurons: FORMULAS
                          f_bh(x) = W_bh . [x, max(0, x - t1), ..., max(0, x - t5)]           # per feature, 5 thresholds
    class scores     = ParT_downstream(o)   # fixed arithmetic: out-projection, LayerNorms, MLP, residuals, final LN, last layer

Exact formulation with the fitted coefficients: S5rp_formulas.py (+ S5rp_model.npz). Each head’s 16 value neurons are written out term by term in its tab.

What it sums over the selected particles: the 16 value neurons

How to read a neuron: neuron = Σ over every particle i of the jet of αi · f(particle i) + c · αcls + b. f is the function written below, evaluated on that particle’s inputs; αi is this head’s weight for that particle in this jet (the weights of all particles and the class token sum to 1, so it is a weighted average). All 16 neurons of a head share the same weights α and differ in f: 16 properties averaged over the same selection.

inputs by total weight:
ln(1 + pT rank)
pT share in prong
ΔR nearest lepton
ΔR
ΔR hardest
ΔR 2nd hardest

What it sums over the selected particles: the 16 value neurons

How to read a neuron: neuron = Σ over every particle i of the jet of αi · f(particle i) + c · αcls + b. f is the function written below, evaluated on that particle’s inputs; αi is this head’s weight for that particle in this jet (the weights of all particles and the class token sum to 1, so it is a weighted average). All 16 neurons of a head share the same weights α and differ in f: 16 properties averaged over the same selection.

What it sums over the selected particles: the 16 value neurons

How to read a neuron: neuron = Σ over every particle i of the jet of αi · f(particle i) + c · αcls + b. f is the function written below, evaluated on that particle’s inputs; αi is this head’s weight for that particle in this jet (the weights of all particles and the class token sum to 1, so it is a weighted average). All 16 neurons of a head share the same weights α and differ in f: 16 properties averaged over the same selection.

What it sums over the selected particles: the 16 value neurons

How to read a neuron: neuron = Σ over every particle i of the jet of αi · f(particle i) + c · αcls + b. f is the function written below, evaluated on that particle’s inputs; αi is this head’s weight for that particle in this jet (the weights of all particles and the class token sum to 1, so it is a weighted average). All 16 neurons of a head share the same weights α and differ in f: 16 properties averaged over the same selection.

What it sums over the selected particles: the 16 value neurons

How to read a neuron: neuron = Σ over every particle i of the jet of αi · f(particle i) + c · αcls + b. f is the function written below, evaluated on that particle’s inputs; αi is this head’s weight for that particle in this jet (the weights of all particles and the class token sum to 1, so it is a weighted average). All 16 neurons of a head share the same weights α and differ in f: 16 properties averaged over the same selection.

What it sums over the selected particles: the 16 value neurons

How to read a neuron: neuron = Σ over every particle i of the jet of αi · f(particle i) + c · αcls + b. f is the function written below, evaluated on that particle’s inputs; αi is this head’s weight for that particle in this jet (the weights of all particles and the class token sum to 1, so it is a weighted average). All 16 neurons of a head share the same weights α and differ in f: 16 properties averaged over the same selection.

What it sums over the selected particles: the 16 value neurons

How to read a neuron: neuron = Σ over every particle i of the jet of αi · f(particle i) + c · αcls + b. f is the function written below, evaluated on that particle’s inputs; αi is this head’s weight for that particle in this jet (the weights of all particles and the class token sum to 1, so it is a weighted average). All 16 neurons of a head share the same weights α and differ in f: 16 properties averaged over the same selection.

What it sums over the selected particles: the 16 value neurons

How to read a neuron: neuron = Σ over every particle i of the jet of αi · f(particle i) + c · αcls + b. f is the function written below, evaluated on that particle’s inputs; αi is this head’s weight for that particle in this jet (the weights of all particles and the class token sum to 1, so it is a weighted average). All 16 neurons of a head share the same weights α and differ in f: 16 properties averaged over the same selection.

inputs by total weight:
ΔR nearest displaced
ΔR nearest photon
ΔR hardest
pT share within 0.1
ln(1 + pT rank)
pT share within 0.2

What it sums over the selected particles: the 16 value neurons

How to read a neuron: neuron = Σ over every particle i of the jet of αi · f(particle i) + c · αcls + b. f is the function written below, evaluated on that particle’s inputs; αi is this head’s weight for that particle in this jet (the weights of all particles and the class token sum to 1, so it is a weighted average). All 16 neurons of a head share the same weights α and differ in f: 16 properties averaged over the same selection.

What it sums over the selected particles: the 16 value neurons

How to read a neuron: neuron = Σ over every particle i of the jet of αi · f(particle i) + c · αcls + b. f is the function written below, evaluated on that particle’s inputs; αi is this head’s weight for that particle in this jet (the weights of all particles and the class token sum to 1, so it is a weighted average). All 16 neurons of a head share the same weights α and differ in f: 16 properties averaged over the same selection.

What it sums over the selected particles: the 16 value neurons

How to read a neuron: neuron = Σ over every particle i of the jet of αi · f(particle i) + c · αcls + b. f is the function written below, evaluated on that particle’s inputs; αi is this head’s weight for that particle in this jet (the weights of all particles and the class token sum to 1, so it is a weighted average). All 16 neurons of a head share the same weights α and differ in f: 16 properties averaged over the same selection.

What it sums over the selected particles: the 16 value neurons

How to read a neuron: neuron = Σ over every particle i of the jet of αi · f(particle i) + c · αcls + b. f is the function written below, evaluated on that particle’s inputs; αi is this head’s weight for that particle in this jet (the weights of all particles and the class token sum to 1, so it is a weighted average). All 16 neurons of a head share the same weights α and differ in f: 16 properties averaged over the same selection.

What it sums over the selected particles: the 16 value neurons

How to read a neuron: neuron = Σ over every particle i of the jet of αi · f(particle i) + c · αcls + b. f is the function written below, evaluated on that particle’s inputs; αi is this head’s weight for that particle in this jet (the weights of all particles and the class token sum to 1, so it is a weighted average). All 16 neurons of a head share the same weights α and differ in f: 16 properties averaged over the same selection.

What it sums over the selected particles: the 16 value neurons

How to read a neuron: neuron = Σ over every particle i of the jet of αi · f(particle i) + c · αcls + b. f is the function written below, evaluated on that particle’s inputs; αi is this head’s weight for that particle in this jet (the weights of all particles and the class token sum to 1, so it is a weighted average). All 16 neurons of a head share the same weights α and differ in f: 16 properties averaged over the same selection.

What it sums over the selected particles: the 16 value neurons

How to read a neuron: neuron = Σ over every particle i of the jet of αi · f(particle i) + c · αcls + b. f is the function written below, evaluated on that particle’s inputs; αi is this head’s weight for that particle in this jet (the weights of all particles and the class token sum to 1, so it is a weighted average). All 16 neurons of a head share the same weights α and differ in f: 16 properties averaged over the same selection.

What it sums over the selected particles: the 16 value neurons

How to read a neuron: neuron = Σ over every particle i of the jet of αi · f(particle i) + c · αcls + b. f is the function written below, evaluated on that particle’s inputs; αi is this head’s weight for that particle in this jet (the weights of all particles and the class token sum to 1, so it is a weighted average). All 16 neurons of a head share the same weights α and differ in f: 16 properties averaged over the same selection.

Definitions of the per-particle inputs

inputin wordsdefinition (math)
ln pThow hard particle i is (its transverse momentum, log)ln pT_i
ln Eits energy (log)ln E_i
ln pT/pT_jetthe fraction of the jet’s pT carried by particle i (log)ln(pT_i / pT_jet)
ln E/E_jetthe fraction of the jet’s energy carried by particle i (log)ln(E_i / E_jet)
ΔRhow far particle i is from the jet axis (the jet’s direction)ΔR_i = √(Δη_i² + Δφ_i²), to the jet axis
Δηits offset from the jet axis in pseudorapidityη_i − η_jet
Δφits offset from the jet axis in azimuthφ_i − φ_jet
chargethe electric charge of particle iq_i ∈ {−1, 0, +1}
charged hadronis particle i a charged hadron (e.g. a pion)?1 if particle i is a charged hadron, else 0
neutral hadronis it a neutral hadron?1 if a neutral hadron
photonis it a photon?1 if a photon
electronis it an electron?1 if an electron
muonis it a muon?1 if a muon
tanh d0how far particle i’s track misses the collision point, sideways — large for tracks from a b or c hadron decaytanh(d0_i), d0 the transverse impact parameter
σ(d0)the uncertainty of that miss distancemin(σ(d0_i), 1)
tanh dzhow far its track misses the collision point along the beamtanh(dz_i), dz the longitudinal impact parameter
σ(dz)the uncertainty of thatmin(σ(dz_i), 1)
ln(1 + pT rank)where particle i stands in the jet’s pT ordering: 0 for the hardest, larger for softer particlesln(1 + r_i), r_i = 0 for the hardest particle of the jet, 1 for the next, …
ln(1+n within 0.1)how many other particles of the jet are within ΔR 0.1 of particle i (a tight cone around it)ln(1 + #{j ≠ i : ΔR_ij < 0.1})
ln(1+n within 0.2)the same within ΔR 0.2ln(1 + #{j ≠ i : ΔR_ij < 0.2})
pT share within 0.1what fraction of the jet’s pT sits in the other particles within ΔR 0.1 of particle i — is i inside a dense, hard core?Σ_{j ≠ i, ΔR_ij < 0.1} pT_j / Σ_j pT_j
pT share within 0.2the same within ΔR 0.2Σ_{j ≠ i, ΔR_ij < 0.2} pT_j / Σ_j pT_j
pT share within 0.4the same within ΔR 0.4Σ_{j ≠ i, ΔR_ij < 0.4} pT_j / Σ_j pT_j
ΔR nearestthe angle from particle i to the closest other particle of the jet — is i isolated or in a cluster?min_{j ≠ i} ΔR_ij (capped at 1.5)
ln pT nearest / pThow hard that closest other particle is compared with particle iln(pT_nn(i) / pT_i), nn(i) the nearest other particle (clipped to ±10)
ΔR hardestthe angle from particle i to the hardest particle of the jetΔR between i and the hardest particle of the jet (capped at 1.5)
ΔR 2nd hardestthe angle from particle i to the second-hardest particleΔR between i and the second-hardest particle (capped at 1.5)
ΔR nearest displacedthe angle from particle i to the closest OTHER particle of the jet that is a displaced track (charged, its track misses the collision point by more than 3σ — typical of b/c-hadron decays). Small: i sits next to a secondary vertex. 1.5 if the jet has no displaced track.min ΔR_ij over the other particles j that are charged and displaced: q_j ≠ 0 and |d0_j| / σ(d0_j) > 3; 1.5 if the jet has none
ΔR nearest leptonthe angle from particle i to the closest other electron or muon in the jet (1.5 if none)min ΔR_ij over the other particles j that are electrons or muons; 1.5 if none
ΔR nearest photonthe angle from particle i to the closest other photon in the jet (1.5 if none)min ΔR_ij over the other photons j; 1.5 if none
prong indexwhich of the jet’s 3 prongs particle i belongs to (the prongs are seeded by the 3 hardest particles; each particle joins the nearest seed): 0, 1 or 2k ∈ {0, 1, 2}: the 3 hardest particles seed 3 prongs; every particle belongs to the prong whose seed is nearest in ΔR; k is the index of particle i’s prong (0 = the hardest seed)
prong pT sharethe fraction of the jet’s pT in particle i’s prongΣ_{j ∈ prong(i)} pT_j / Σ_j pT_j
prong ln massthe mass of particle i’s prong (log)ln(1 + m(prong(i))), the invariant mass of the summed 4-vectors of the prong’s particles
prong chargethe total charge of particle i’s prongΣ_{j ∈ prong(i)} q_j
prong n displacedhow many displaced tracks are in particle i’s prong#{j ∈ prong(i) : q_j ≠ 0, |d0_j| / σ(d0_j) > 3}
pT share in prongthe fraction of its prong’s pT that particle i carries — the prong’s leader or a soft companion?pT_i / Σ_{j ∈ prong(i)} pT_j
ΔR prong axisthe angle from particle i to the seed (hardest particle) of its prongΔR between i and the seed particle of its prong (capped at 1.5)
ln kT with nearesthow hard and wide the splitting between particle i and its closest neighbour is (kT = softer pT × angle)ln(min(pT_i, pT_nn(i)) · ΔR_i,nn(i))

Every input describes one particle i of the jet — the particle a head is summing over. “Nearest” always means nearest to particle i, among the other particles of the same jet, by the angle ΔR = √(Δη² + Δφ²).

Context seen through ParT’s pair kernels: ParT adds to every particle-attention logit a learned bias U_h(i, j) = f_h(ln kT_ij, ln z_ij, ln ΔR_ij, ln m²_ij), one per head h = 1…8 (kT_ij = min(pT_i, pT_j)·ΔR_ij, z_ij = min(pT_i, pT_j)/(pT_i + pT_j), m_ij the pair mass). With w_hij = softmax_j U_h(i, j) over the other particles, “hk: P” = Σ_{j ≠ i} w_hij P_j for the property P of particle j (ln pT_j/pT_jet, q_j, its type, tanh d0_j, [charged and |d0_j|/σ > 3], ΔR_j to the axis), and “hk: ln ΔR to i” = Σ_j w_hij ln ΔR_ij.

Code: jetdistill/part/clsfit.py (particle_features), jetdistill/research/nbr.py (nbr_features, pk_features).
